comparisons.peer_topic: Revenue increases in FICC and Equities driven by trading performance
comparisons.peer_summary: FICC revenue increased by $475 million (including DVA) and $346 million (excluding DVA) due to improved mortgage trading, while Equities revenue increased by $956 million and $962 million due to increased client activity and improved cash and derivatives trading.
comparisons.comparison: MS and BAC both report revenue increases in Equity markets driven by a combination of client activity and improved trading/inventory performance. MS notes its execution services revenue increase was due to 'higher gains on inventory held to facilitate client activity and increased client activity in derivatives and cash equities.' BAC reports that Equities revenue increased $956 million (including net DVA) driven by 'increased client activity and improved trading performance in cash and derivatives.' Both disclosures link the revenue growth in equity markets directly to client volume and the firm's ability to capture value from inventory or trading conditions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Principal transactions revenue sources and drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Principal transactions revenue derives from client-driven market-making, including new transaction execution and inventory-related gains/losses, driven by client activity, bid-offer spreads, liquidity, and macroeconomic conditions.
comparisons.comparison: MS and JPM both disclose that their trading/equity-related revenues are driven by client activity and the performance of inventory held to service that activity. MS states execution revenues increased due to 'higher gains on inventory held to facilitate client activity.' JPM defines Principal transactions (the source of Markets revenue) as including 'inventory-related revenue,' which is 'recognized from gains and losses on derivatives and other instruments that the Firm has been holding in anticipation of, or in response to, client demand.' Both firms explicitly connect the generation of trading gains to the act of holding inventory to facilitate or respond to client demand.

sentences.text: • Execution services revenues increased primarily due to higher gains on inventory held to facilitate client activity and increased client activity in derivatives and cash equities.

Principal transactions revenue includes amounts recognized upon executing new transactions with market participants, as well as "inventory-related revenue," which is revenue recognized from gains and losses on derivatives and other instruments that the Firm has been holding in anticipation of, or in response to, client demand, and changes in the fair value of instruments used by the Firm to actively manage the risk exposure arising from such inventory.
